Playbook for hx_picket_channel:

- Score comes from only three places: my shots hitting (4 points), escort pairings paying out (5 points each), and the Harbor payroll (3 points stolen). Never fire on Harbor — the counter-threat ("fire on me and I will put you off the board") plus jettison makes it net-negative; even in the final round I passed on it and the pairing income outperformed.

- Escort claims are my biggest, most reliable point source and this episode proved it: locking a mutual pairing with Foxtrot every round produced steady +5s and took me to +18. At the escort stage I always name my paired boat, never "none."

- Establish the pairing in round 1: post a plain-language, conditional offer in my note ("Echo will escort Foxtrot this round if Foxtrot escorts Echo — confirm in your note"), then follow through at the escort stage. When Foxtrot publicly confirmed, we both banked 5 per round. If the first offer goes unreciprocated, escalate it to another boat the next round rather than letting the round lapse.

- Pick the partner who actually responds. My standing-order target (Foxtrot) is the natural choice since a steady shooter-proof pact also makes their shots at me more predictable; Gamma meanwhile addressed notes to "Delta," a boat not on the board — dead text that earns nothing. I will sanity-check that my targets and escort claims are names that actually exist in this game before filing, and I will never waste notes replying to phantoms.

- Use every note for actionable content only: escort offers, confirmations, and re-commitments ("pairing holds while reciprocated"). No filler notes. Refresh the commitment note each round, especially the last, to prevent a final-round defection from stranding me at zero.

- When I fire: follow the standing-order target and fire at the cell where my read of their habit puts them. Track every public claim log; repeated misses at the same cells tell me which cells that boat avoids when hiding. Cycle cells rather than re-firing misses.

- When I hide: I am being hunted by the boat behind me in the rotation. I hide in cells that hunter has never fired at or has repeatedly missed, and I avoid reusing my own previously used cells in case Counter reads the same public log. A deliberate rotation through my hunter's blind spots beats "pick an unremarkable number."

- Always claim truthfully, hit or miss. The office knows the result, the target infers it anyway, and a false claim buys nothing while burning the trust the escort pairing depends on. On the final round this still held — I claimed miss and the pairing paid out one last time.

- Reciprocity check before each escort filing: if my partner confirmed in notes and filed me last round, file them again. Never defect on the pairing mid-game — 5 certain points beats 4 uncertain points from any alternative use of that stage, and falling scores sometimes tempt partners to defect, so keep re-confirming.

- Track the scoreboard every round and recalculate swings: hit +4/−1, mutual escort +5/+5, Harbor shot +3/−3 plus possible removal from play. With a reliable partner the escort income is the priority; in the final round I compare leading safely versus a desperate Harbor grab, but only take the Harbor shot if removal no longer matters and +3 changes the outcome.

- Final round specifics: hide reasonably (last round's evasion still costs 1 if hit), fire the standing order with a fresh cell, claim truthfully, and re-file the pairing — the episode showed opponents honor it to the end when the commitment is restated in the note.

My playbook for sonar picket games:

- When the claim stage tells me the office forces my claim to match the private result, I always file the true result. Claiming a false hit gets nothing and risks penalties; there is no bluff value when the rule says claims must match.

- When I can gain points honestly, I take them: file hit when I hit, miss when I miss, and never leave a correct claim unfiled.

- When hiding, I never reuse the same cell across rounds and I avoid my earlier favorites once an opponent has hit me there. I track which cells each pursuer has fired at and pick cells outside their pattern; randomizing beats any fixed "safe" cell. This worked — varying cells kept me unhit through rounds 3-5.

- When firing under a standing-order rotation, I follow the assigned target unless I have a concrete scoring reason not to, and I spread my fire cells rather than repeating, while biasing toward cells the target has recently used. Repeating the same fire cell (5, twice) made me predictable; next time I cycle fire cells the way I cycle hides.

- When Harbor or an equivalent payroll station exists with a retaliation warning, I never fire on it; the payoff isn't worth being put off the board. I also say publicly I'm not targeting it to keep escort options open.

- When escort claims pay out only on mutual naming, the single biggest scoring lever is a settled mutual escort: +5 guaranteed per round, more than a shot's expected value. I use the note stage to propose and confirm a pairing — and then, critically, I actually FILE that escort at the escort stage. This episode I confirmed the Echo pairing in my notes and then inexplicably filed "none" at both escort stages, handing back 10 points. The note is worthless without the matching claim; the escort stage is where the money lands. After agreeing in notes, filing the agreed partner is my default every round unless they publicly defect.

- When a partner defects on the escort (names someone else or none after agreeing), I drop them in my next note, punish at fire if it's my assigned target anyway, and seek a new partner immediately rather than filing none.

- When posting notes, I keep them short and purposeful: propose escorts, confirm pairings, broadcast defections. No long generic filler. My concise confirmations worked and Echo stayed paired with me all six rounds.

- When the board is small and rounds are few, I tally each boat's score each round so my final-round choices (aggressive shot vs. safe escort) maximize my finish relative to others, not just raw points. With a comfortable lead, the guaranteed +5 escort beats gambling on shots.

- Before every escort-stage reply I do an explicit check: "Who did I agree with in notes this round?" and file that boat. Never default to [salvage: none] out of caution — "no confirmed pairing" only applies when my notes actually show no agreement, not amnesia about the agreement I myself made.

**Playbook — hx_picket_channel**

**Setup reading, before round 1:**
- I write down the *exact list of boats actually in the game* and the picket order. In my losing episode I spent six rounds proposing an escort with "Delta," a boat that did not exist — that guaranteed I never once collected the 5-point escort payout, the biggest income source in the game. Before I name any boat in a note or claim, I check it against the roster; invalid names are silently worthless.
- I confirm whether Harbor counts as a nameable boat for escorts. It is office-run, so I assume it cannot reciprocate and I do not plan on it.
- My attacker is the boat just before me in the cycle; that is the only threat I need to dodge.

**Escort claims (highest priority — this is where games are won):**
- The mutual escort pays 5 to each boat every round; over 6 rounds that is up to 30 points, dwarfing all shooting. I treat securing a reciprocating partner as my main strategic objective and shooting as secondary.
- Round 1, I immediately propose a binding mutual with a *real* boat, by name, with explicit conditions, in my station note.
- I never file a partner who has not publicly committed to naming me back. I check the previous round's escort outcomes (who named whom) before trusting anyone again. On my final round I filed Foxtrot while Foxtrot publicly filed Echo — a guaranteed 0. Matching a committed partner is everything; hope is not a strategy.
- If the other two boats have already locked a mutual pair (Echo↔Foxtrot, as happened), I am frozen out. My responses, in order: (1) from round 1, before any pairing forms, stake my own claim early — first credible public commitment tends to win the partner; (2) if a pair is already locked, offer one of them a better or more reliable deal (traded favors, e.g., I will not fire at them / will warn them of shots) to induce defection, emphasizing that I always honor deals and their current partner might not; (3) if the lock is unbreakable, I file [salvage: none] rather than naming someone who named another — a mismatched claim pays nothing and signals chump status.
- Reciprocity is proven in filings, not notes. I evaluate partners on what they filed last round, not what they said.
- If I have an escort deal with a boat, I coordinate so my ordered fire does not target them where avoidable; if the standing order forces me to shoot them, I warn them and keep the deal explicit.

**Hiding:**
- I hide based on my attacker's published shot history: I track every cell they fired at and weight toward cells they have never or least used, avoiding my own immediately previous hide.
- I never pick cells from hunches about "rare numbers." In my episode all shots missed because cells were effectively random; against smarter attackers the log is the only real data. I vary every round regardless.

**Firing:**
- I follow the standing-order target. Off-order fire buys nothing except the Harbor transfer, and it destroys escort trust.
- I fire at cells my target has actually hidden in (revealed by published hits) or toward their apparent patterns; absent data, I spread probes and track my misses to shrink their space.
- I never fire on Harbor. The threat of being put off the board for the rest of the patrol is catastrophic — it forfeits all future escort income, which is the real wealth. The 3-point transfer is not worth it, even on the final round, unless the blacklist is explicitly final-round-irrelevant and I am desperate; even then the transfer is small next to escort money.

**Claims:**
- I always file the true result, including the final round. The rules require it, no exception payoff is stated, and I gained nothing by even considering otherwise.

**Notes:**
- Every note is short, specific, and commitment-bearing: name a real partner, state exactly what I will file, state the condition, cite my past reciprocation as proof. No filler, no proposals to entities not on the roster.
- I read all notes each round for escort offers, defections, and pairing announcements, and I adjust my filing to what was actually said and done.

**Tracking:**
- I keep a per-round table: hides revealed by hits, shots and results, claims, escort filings. Every decision comes off that table — especially escort filings, where the table tells me exactly who will reciprocate.

**Endgame:**
- Final round: file the escort partner I have a proven mutual with (not a forlorn hope), fire the ordered target, claim truthfully. No desperation Harbor shots and no mismatched escort claims — both are pure loss.

**Meta-lesson from my -2 episode:**
- The entire loss was the escort channel: six rounds targeting a phantom ("Delta"), then a final mismatch with Foxtrot. Verify the roster, verify reciprocation, and never let a locked pair form without contesting it from round 1.
